title: PlayerHealth
description: Implement a plain C# PlayerHealth class yourself, without Unity or MonoBehaviour. Expose MaxHealth, CurrentHealth, IsDead, TakeDamage(int amount), and Heal(int amount). CurrentHealth must start equal to MaxHealth and always stay between 0 and MaxHealth. Zero or negative damage and zero or negative healing are invalid. CurrentHealth must not be directly modifiable externally. IsDead must be true when CurrentHealth == 0. Check starting health, boundary values, invalid amounts, and external access yourself.
hints: Which parts of the health state should callers be allowed to observe, and which changes should only PlayerHealth control?
Start with the initial health state and external access rules. Before coding the methods, predict what should happen when damage exceeds current health or healing would exceed maximum health.

Encapsulation lets a class protect its own state. Treat the range from zero to MaxHealth as an invariant: every valid operation must preserve it. Reject invalid amounts separately from handling valid amounts that reach a boundary. IsDead describes the current state rather than a separate value that can drift out of sync.

Investigation outline: create an instance; inspect its starting state; choose a normal operation and a boundary case; predict health and death state; invoke the operation; compare observations with the requirements; repeat for healing and invalid amounts. Check separately whether a caller can assign CurrentHealth.
